classification.difficultyReason: Find two intersections algebraically, then compare the line gradient with the tangent gradients to establish a normal relationship.

content.prompt: Find the points where the line $x+2y=4$ cuts the parabola $y=(x-1)^2$. Show that the line is the normal to the curve at one of these points.

spec.description: Equation-driven blue parabola and red descending line, with black arrowed coordinate axes. No grid, numerical ticks, origin label or intersection labels.
spec.mathematics: The parabola y=(x-1)^2 has vertex (1,0). The line x+2y=4 intersects it twice.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied curves, axes and line equation are visible; intersection coordinates and normal justification remain in the answer.

answer.short: Intersections: $\left(-\frac12,\frac94\right)$ and $(2,1)$. The line is normal to the curve at $(2,1)$ because its gradient is $-\frac12$ and the tangent gradient is $2$.
answer.worked:
At an intersection,
$$\begin{align*}
x+2(x-1)^2&=4\\
2x^2-3x-2&=0\\
(2x+1)(x-2)&=0\\
x&=-\frac12\text{ or }2.
\end{align*}$$
Using $y=(x-1)^2$ gives the intersection points $\left(-\frac12,\frac94\right)$ and $(2,1)$.

The line has equation $y=-\frac12x+2$, so its gradient is $-\frac12$.
$$\begin{align*}
f'(x)&=2(x-1)\\
f'(2)&=2\\
m_{\text{line}}m_{\text{tangent}}&=-\frac12\times2\\
&=-1.
\end{align*}$$
The line passes through $(2,1)$ and is perpendicular to the tangent there. Therefore $x+2y=4$ is the normal to the curve at $(2,1)$.
